title: Run: schedule_change_announcement on Cassandra dev@ 2014
description: Implement the schedule_change_announcement binary classifier (single-thesis prompt + structured JSON output + logprobs for calibration), run it over the 731-message Cassandra dev@ 2014 corpus via the homelab Qwen3-Coder endpoint, hand-label a small eval set (~50-100 messages stratified across the year), score through the eval harness, then write the Results block to docs/experiment-log.md and commit. Structural prerequisites: pre-reg must be committed first (si-rn2), eval harness must exist (si-9nr). The Beads dependency edges enforce this — this issue cannot become 'ready' until both are closed.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Detector code lives under src/classify/. (2) Per-run scorecard committed to results/evals/. (3) Results block written to experiment-log.md after the pre-reg block, committed in a separate commit. (4) Surprises (anything contradicting the Prediction) called out explicitly in Results.

title: Pre-register: schedule_change_announcement on Cassandra dev@ 2014
description: Design and commit the Pre-registration block (Setup, Prediction, Decision rule, Falsifiers/mind-changers) to docs/experiment-log.md for the first detector experiment. Closes when the pre-reg block is committed to git. The commit hash should be captured in the closing note as the receipt — this is the structural enforcement of the two-commit pre-reg discipline. Context: first detector run, on the corpus harvested in commit f26ca42 (731 Cassandra dev@ messages, 2014). Detector is the binary classifier 'schedule_change_announcement' from docs/detector-catalog.md. Picked over risk_escalation_language because it's easier to hand-label and exercises the eval harness with less affective ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-registration block exists in docs/experiment-log.md and is committed to git BEFORE any detector code runs against the corpus. The Beads issue close note records the commit hash.

title: Build first eval harness for binary classifiers
description: Stand up the per-component eval scaffolding so detector runs produce calibration data, not just predictions. Should support: (a) loading a small hand-labeled ground truth set, (b) running a classifier over the same items, (c) computing precision/recall/F1 plus calibration (e.g., reliability diagram, Brier score) using the logprobs that the homelab Qwen3 endpoint exposes, (d) writing per-run scorecards to results/evals/. This is upstream of every detector experiment.
acceptance_criteria: Given a labeled JSONL file and a classifier function, produces a scorecard JSON with precision, recall, F1, Brier score, and a reliability-bin breakdown. Scorecard committed to results/evals/ with provenance (model id, prompt hash, timestamp).

title: Harvest a second multi-org corpus
description: The Cassandra dev@ 2014 corpus we have is single-org-dominant (Datastax + core committers do ~80% of volume), so multi-vendor coordination detectors (vendor_silence, blame_displacement, vendor_status_update) cannot be meaningfully tested on it. We need at least one corpus where the vendor-coordination texture actually exists. UNDER-SPECIFIED: which corpus? Candidates to evaluate: (a) Hadoop dev@ — multi-org Apache TLP with strong commercial-vendor presence (Cloudera, Hortonworks, Yahoo). (b) An Apache Incubator project that retired (gives clean failure-outcome label). (c) IETF working group archive — deferred earlier because the export endpoint requires login, but worth re-examining if the static browse path can be scraped. Picking the right one is itself work. Surfaces from the harvest entry in docs/experiment-log.md (2026-05-01).
acceptance_criteria: (1) Decision documented in docs/datasets.md or experiment-log.md noting which corpus and why. (2) Harvester runs successfully against it, producing JSONL under data/processed/. (3) Sender-affiliation diversity verified (top-10 senders span 3+ distinct organizations).
